title: Stability simulation runbook and variant playlist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook for the stability simulation week (internal name: sim-week-iv). Goal is to exercise variant rollouts, throttles, and rollback criteria for the new routing and KV-cache changes landing in release v2.8. This doc bundles the scenario matrix, day-by-day calendar, operator checklists, smoke tests, and a first-pass release notes draft for the incident/upgrade narrative.

Quick primer (TL;DR):
- Week objective: validate canary->wave rollouts with traffic shaping and circuit breakers under modest injected failures (latency & GPU OOM).
- Target environments: staging-ops, perf-lab, canary-prod (1%), regional-bands us-west/us-east-eu-central.
- Primary metrics: p50/p95 latency, success_rate (200/200 2xx vs 5xx), model-token-cost-per-req, kv-hit-rate, gpu-util spike patterns.

Open questions (to resolve before sim start):
- Who owns mid-rollout hotfix deploys? (Ops lead + code owner pair?) 
- Final canary metric thresholds (p95 percent increase allowed) — propose 20% p95 and 1.5x error budget burn in 15m window.
- Circuit breaker timeout values: default 10s vs 6s for latency-sensitive routes.

Simulation matrix (scenarios):
1) Baseline smoke: full traffic to staging-ops + perf synthetic load (no failure). Validate metrics baseline and telemetry tags.
2) Slow upstream: add 250–500ms per-token penalty on model shard A. Watch p95 and retry amplification. Expected action: reduce canary weight to 0 for that variant and fallback routing.
3) KV cache miss storm: purge cache in perf-lab; simulate 3x fewer kv-hits. Observe per-token token-cost and tail latency. Expected action: enable short-term prefix cache warming and throttle burst traffic.
4) GPU OOM injection: simulate OOM on 1 GPU in canary-prod. Expected action: auto-failover to next pool, record rollback if error rate > threshold.
5) Dependent service outage: vector-store read failures ~10% requests for 30m. Observe downstream error propagation. Expected action: degrade to condensed embeddings path and enable graceful degradation message on client.
6) Network partition: isolate eu-central region for 45m to test cross-region fallback. Expected action: route to us-east with region-tagging and SLA notification.

Variant playlist (priority order for exercises):
- variant-a: v2.8-default (new routing + kv-cache)
- variant-b: v2.8-quantized (lower mem, unknown perf tail)
- variant-c: v2.7-stable (fallback)
- variant-d: experimental-batching (disabled by default)

Calendar (compact run plan):
Day -3: preflight and smoke in staging-ops. Owners: Marcus (observability), Ana (serving). Checklist below.
Day -2: perf-lab burst tests + instrumentation verification. Owners: Priya + Ethan.
Day -1: dry-run release to canary-prod (0.1%) at 09:00 UTC — verify dashboards and alerting.
Sim Day 0: escalate to 1% canary at 09:30, then staged wave to 5%/20%/60% over 6h windows if metrics green. Inject scenario 2 at 11:00.
Sim Day 1: stress tests and OOM injection at 10:00, KV purge at 14:00. Postmortem notes and release notes drafting in afternoon.
Sim Day 2: rollback rehearsals, rollback automation trigger checks, finalize rollout checklist and release notes.

Operator checklists (preflight):
- Confirm dashboards: latency (p50/p95), errors (500/429/504), token-cost, kv-hit-rate, queue-depths.
- Alerting: ensure slack/ops pager routes enabled for each alert channel.
- Backout plan: clear rollback button available in console; rollback owner assigned + on-call.
- Traffic steering: feature-flag toggles verified and accessible (QA: toggles/weights can be toggled within 30s).
- Canary capacity: ensure dedicated pool has 20% spare GPU headroom.
- Dependencies: vector-store replicas healthy and redis kv nodes at <70% mem.

During rollout (operator playbook):
- At each weight step (0.1 -> 1 -> 5 -> 20 -> 60):
  * Wait 15 minutes after traffic settle before judging metrics.
  * Check error budget burn; if >30% of budget in 15m, pause and drop to previous weight.
  * If p95 increases >20% absolute or error rate >0.5%, run immediate smoke test (single request sequence) and escalate to on-call.
  * Record snapshot: grafana url, last 15m percentiles, sample traces, last deploy artifact sha.

Rollback triggers (formalized):
- Rapid error spike: sustained >0.5% 5xx for 10m.
- Latency regression: p95 > baseline*1.2 for two consecutive 15m windows.
- Cost regression: per-request token cost >1.5x baseline for 30m.
- Manual: critical customer reports (CS triage) or SRE judgement.

Rollback procedure (quick steps):
1) Flip feature flag to route all new traffic to fallback variant (v2.7-stable).
2) Trigger rollback job in console (rollback collects event id).
3) If job fails, scale pool down and reassign requests to stable pool manually.
4) Post-rollback: run minimal regression smoke tests and keep canary at 0 for 2h before reattempt.
5) Open incident note and assign postmortem owner.

Smoke tests (automated probe sequences):
- Chat sequence: short prompt -> tool call -> streaming output -> finalization. (Check latency and completeness)
- Embedding path: document -> 512-dim vector -> vector-store upsert -> query -> similarity top1 == expected.
- Authz path: token impersonation check + audit log write.

Telemetry capture & retrospective artifacts:
- Must capture: request-id, model-shard-id, pool-id, variant-id, kv-hit boolean, token-count, trace_id.
- Snapshot storage: s3://sim-week-artifacts/{run_id}/ with compressed traces and sample responses.
- Retrospective template to include: timeline, decisions, metric deltas, owner notes, top 3 action items.

Draft release notes (placeholders):
- Header: Release v2.8 — routing and cache improvements (simulation week).
- Summary: Adds smarter routing that falls back to lower-memory model variants and improves prefix KV cache warmup for bursty workloads.
- User impact: No visible API changes. Expect lower latency variance and reduced token-cost for repeat prefixes.
- Known issues: quantized variant may show higher p95 on certain token-length distributions; we will roll as opt-in for customers on Dedicated pools.

Communication templates (short):
- Slack ops channel: @here sim-week-iv starting 09:00 UTC. Expect temporary routing experiments; report any 5xxs in #ops-incident.
- Customer note (if degradation > 30m): "We're investigating increased request latency for some requests (affecting ~X%). We're rolling back and will update in 30 minutes."

Notes to self (rough, informal):
- Priya: validate that the rollback job preserves correlation ids (we lost them in last attempt — caused tracing gaps).
- Marcus: add a short-lived metric for "kv-priming-success" to track prefix warms.
- Ana: confirm canary alert suppression rules avoid noisy pagering for transient blips under 3m.

Post-sim deliverables (owners):
- Incident/experiment write-up (Priya) — include traces + sample responses.
- Follow-up action items with owners and due dates (Marcus/Ana/Ethan).
- Update runbook to include circuit-breaker tuning values and canary % defaults.

Appendix: quick links and tickets
- Observability board: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/ops/sim-week-dashboard
- Run artifacts s3: s3://sim-week-artifacts/run-2024-11-18
- Jira experiment epic: JIRA-RELE-789 (contains smaller task tickets)
- GH PR for rollout automation: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412

End of draft — rough and intentionally chatty. Will convert to a formal release playbook after sim-week with annotated screenshots and finalized thresholds.
